**Perforeret ulcus** (perforated ulcer) is a life-threatening medical condition tracked within the Danish Acute Surgery Database (Akut Kirurgi Databasen) [^src1]. It is specifically monitored under Indicator 4x, a national quality metric dedicated to time-critical, life-threatening surgical emergencies such as perforations and ischemia [^src1]. 

The primary clinical significance of a perforated ulcer is its severe time dependency. Evidence highlights that the probability of patient survival drops by 2.4% for every hour of delay in surgical intervention [^src1]. This stark statistic underscores the report's observation that survival rates continually decline as time passes, providing the clinical justification for the strict time targets mandated by Indicator 4x [^src1].

Within the broader context of Danish healthcare, tracking conditions like perforeret ulcus is part of an annual national quality monitoring initiative published by the Danish Healthcare Quality Programme. Data on these time-based indicators is used to evaluate regional performance, identify systemic bottlenecks such as a lack of operating room capacity, and recognize local best practices like those in the North Denmark Region [^src1]. Ultimately, the clinical evidence surrounding perforated ulcers supports political and administrative decisions regarding resource allocation and process optimization in acute surgery [^src1].
